additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food in a discrete period while experiencing a sense of loss of control, followed by marked distress such as shame, guilt, or disgust. Unlike Bulimia Nervosa, it is not regularly accompanied by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise. It is commonly associated with obesity or weight fluctuations, body image concerns, and mood or anxiety symptoms, and often follows a chronic, fluctuating course that can be exacerbated by stress, dieting, and emotional triggers. Onset can occur in adolescence or adulthood and is frequently linked to attempts at rigid dietary restraint, emotional coping through food, or longstanding patterns of using eating to manage distress.

patient.personality: Richard is a disciplined, detail-oriented retiree who prefers structured routines, quiet intellectual pursuits, and carefully planned community projects over spontaneity or emotional display.
patient.stressor: Following his formal retirement and the winding down of his small business responsibilities, Richard’s days became far less structured, leaving him with long stretches of unplanned time despite his volunteering at the historical society. He initially enjoyed the freedom to read, cook, and attend cultural events, but he also felt a subtle loss of identity and purpose that he was reluctant to admit, even to his wife. Over the next year, he began to rely more on solitary evening meals and snacks in front of his reading or television as a way to fill time and soothe a vague restlessness, gradually abandoning the slower, ritualized meals he once prided himself on preparing. When he noticed that he was starting to eat very quickly during these periods, barely registering the food and feeling oddly unsettled afterward, he became concerned that this new pattern was out of character and mentioned it to his primary care doctor, who referred him for psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately I’ve been eating much faster than I ever used to, almost like I’m rushing through my meals without thinking.”

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: In the evenings, especially when my wife goes to bed early and I'm alone with a book or the television, I can go through a full plate of leftovers, half a loaf of bread with butter, a big bowl of cereal, and then ice cream on top of that in one sitting, easily two or three times what I would have considered a normal meal when I was still working.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like something just takes over and I keep opening the fridge and piling more on my plate even while I'm telling myself, almost scolding myself, that I should stop.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I used to take pride in savoring my cooking, but now I find myself shoveling it in so fast that by the time the news program is halfway through, my plate is already cleared and I barely remember tasting the food.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: There are many nights when I've already had a perfectly adequate dinner, I’m not the least bit hungry, and yet I’ll still get up during a documentary or while I’m reading and raid the pantry for crackers, cheese, cookies—whatever’s there—until I feel uncomfortably full.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: After these episodes, when I finally switch off the TV and see the empty containers and crumbs around my chair, I feel foolish and ashamed, like a man who should know better but keeps sneaking food like a teenager, and I lie in bed replaying it and promising myself I won’t do it again.
